# l2disco — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E2 A2 H1 P3 · limited by scope (core), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — gopacket v1.7.5 `layers` (LLDP, CDP, ARP, DHCPv4/v6, ICMPv6 ND), insomniacslk/dhcp (DHCPv4/v6 option set) and lldpd 1.0.22 docs (LLDP/CDP) (surveyed 2026-11-04)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-04 · mutation 2026-10-04 (34/34) · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-10-09 (200,000-run budget per harness clean, L2DISCO_FUZZ) · ct n/a — LLDP/CDP codec (keyword review, 2026-10-07) · panic 2026-10-31 (sweep + blind review: caller-input asserts → checked panics, `arp.Packet.encode` → `EncodeError`, iterators end after the first error, CDP checksum u64; delta audit 28/29 + 1 eq)

**Performance:** ref 0.02–0.56× Go gopacket v1.7.5 (default configuration, decode only; lldp 0.04 and cdp 0.02 are library-path vs allocation-free-path, not parser-for-parser; arp 0.40, dhcp4 0.38, dhcp6 0.50, nd_ra 0.56) · fastest: gopacket on the DHCP rows (insomniacslk/dhcp is 46x (dhcp4) and 79x (dhcp6) slower than ours, 17x and 39x slower than gopacket), not measured for LLDP/CDP/ARP/ND (measured 2026-11-04, `zig build bench-l2disco -Djcc-safe`, 9 rounds, spreads up to 15 % on a shared host)

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** yes

Design + threat notes for auditors. Usage: see ./README.md. Attribution/provenance: see this module's `NOTICE` (vendored tcpdump capture frames).

**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig LLDP+CDP+ARP+DHCPv4+DHCPv6 codec we found — allocation-free, builders as well as parsers, strict-by-default with opt-in tolerance that reports what was dropped, and checked against 15 real frames from tcpdump's dissector suite including four upstream crash reproducers. **Where we are behind** (re-checked 2026-11-04): typed decoding of the rarer org TLVs (802.1Qbg, DCBX, Profinet, Cisco-OUI PoE, 802.1 protocol identity / VID usage digest / management VID / link aggregation), the vendor CDP TLVs beyond the nine typed ones, the other vendor discovery protocols (EDP/FDP/SONMP) and builders for most org TLVs (all consciously rejected or deferred below). Built since the survey: LLDP-MED, 802.3 power, DHCPv4 options 42/43/60/66/67/82/119/121, ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery (2026-10-04); DHCPv6 (RFC 8415) and LLDP-MED location content (coordinate, civic, ELIN) (2026-11-04).

**Survey verdicts 2026-11-04** (gopacket v1.7.2/v1.7.5 `layers` and insomniacslk/dhcp read at the feature-list level; every feature a user would notice). *Done:* DHCPv6 (`dhcp6`: ids, IA_NA/TA/PD, IAADDR, prefix, prefix exclude, status, FQDN, vendor/user class, reconfigure, DNS/SNTP/domain list, relay); LLDP-MED location content (coordinate, civic, ELIN); 802.1 link aggregation (and the deprecated 802.3 copy), protocol identity, VID usage digest, management VID (all four exist in gopacket's `Decode8021`/`Decode8023`, verified in its source); CDP typed MTU, power consumption, system name, extended trust, untrusted CoS. *Rejected, with the reason:* 802.1Qbg (EVB/CDCP: data-centre bridge control, a state machine's input, not a neighbour record; raw via `OrgIterator`); DCBX and Profinet and Cisco-OUI PoE (vendor TLV sets whose meaning depends on the sender's firmware; no public stable spec we can check against); CDP VLAN reply/query, location, PoE request/available, spare-pair PoE, EnergyWise, IP prefixes, hello and SysOID (Cisco-proprietary structures reverse-engineered by gopacket itself; we have no spec or oracle to verify a decode against, so we expose the raw value through `TlvIterator` rather than guess); EDP/FDP/SONMP (lldpd only, vendor protocols retired by their owners); MLD, STP, VRRP, EAPOL and the other 100+ gopacket layers (not neighbour discovery; no sibling module exists). *Sibling-owned:* Ethernet/IP/UDP header peeling (the caller; this is a payload codec), address text (`netaddr`). The typed DHCPv6 options in insomniacslk/dhcp beyond those above (boot file URL, ARCH type, SIP, NTP etc.) pass through `Message.option` raw: each is a flat value with no framing beyond the option header.

## Design & invariants

- **Five submodules, one MAC helper:** `lldp` (802.1AB LLDPDU 7-bit-type/9-bit-length TLV stream:
  mandatory Chassis ID / Port ID / TTL / End, optional descriptions/capabilities/management
  address, org-specific type-127 with 802.1 + 802.3 decoding), `cdp` (version/holdtime/checksum
  header + type/length TLVs, RFC 1071 checksum compute/verify), `arp` (RFC 826 generic `Packet` +
  typed Ethernet+IPv4 `EthIpv4` request/reply/gratuitous/probe), `dhcp` (RFC 2131 header + magic
  cookie + RFC 2132 options), `mac` (48-bit EUI-48 parse/format + broadcast/multicast/local
  predicates). Modeled after IEEE 802.1AB, Cisco CDP (reverse-engineered reference), RFC 826, RFC
  2131/2132 — see NOTICE for clean-room provenance.
- **Allocation-free hot path:** parse iterators slice the input buffer (values borrow it); builders
  write into a caller-provided buffer. No sockets, no syscalls — codec only.
- **Forward-compatible parsing:** unknown optional TLVs/options pass through raw and never fail the
  parse; every length is bounds-checked against the buffer.
- **Concurrency:** reentrant — no shared state; safe if instances are not shared.
- **Error policy:** malformed or truncated input is a typed error, never a panic.
- **Opt-in tolerance, strict by default:** `lldp.ParseOptions.tolerant_optionals` and
  `cdp.ParseOptions.tolerant_trailing_tlv` (both default `false`) let a caller keep a frame whose
  data loss is confined to a TLV that was never load-bearing for identifying the neighbour, instead
  of discarding the whole record. `lldp`: a malformed *optional* TLV (System Capabilities of the
  wrong length, an internally-inconsistent Management Address) is skipped and
  `Lldpdu.skipped_optionals` counts how many; the mandatory trio (Chassis ID, Port ID, TTL) and its
  ordering always still fail the parse outright, in both modes — that is the actual identity of the
  neighbour and losing it silently would be worse than losing the frame. `cdp`: a truncated/malformed
  *trailing* TLV — the shape real 802.3 zero-padding to the 60-byte minimum frame produces once the
  walk reaches it — stops the walk and keeps what parsed instead of failing the whole frame;
  `Frame.trailing_tlv_truncated` reports whether this happened. Both flags surface *that* something
  was dropped (a count / a bool) rather than dropping it silently, on the reasoning that the finding
  which motivated them was itself "the module silently threw away a good neighbour" — the fix must
  not create the same failure mode in the other direction for a caller that cares.

## LLDP-MED, DHCP options, ND (2026-10-04)

- **LLDP-MED / power** decode in `OrgSpecific.decode` under OUI 00-12-BB (TIA-1057 subtypes 1-11)
  and 00-12-0F subtype 2 (power via MDI; the 802.3at fields are read only when all 5 extra octets
  are present — a shorter TLV is the 802.3ab form, not a truncated 802.3at one). A TLV too short
  for its fixed fields stays undecoded (null), never an error: org TLVs are optional and vendors
  pad them oddly. Network policy's 24-bit field is unpacked as U(1) T(1) X(1) VLAN(12) prio(3)
  DSCP(6).
- **DHCP 82, 119 and 121** are validated lazily, by their iterators (sub-option framing; RFC 3442
  width 0-32 and the significant-octet count; RFC 1035 labels), never by `Message.parse`: a
  malformed sub-structure must not hide the rest of the message — axp's rogue-DHCP check needs the
  server id of an OFFER whose option 121 is garbage (a review finding against this change's first
  draft, which failed the whole parse). `DomainSearchIterator`'s whose compression pointers must point strictly
  backwards (no loop is possible) and whose names are bounded at 254 characters. The builders
  never compress (every receiver must accept uncompressed names).
- **ND** validates option framing at parse (length 0 is an error, RFC 4861 §4.6) and leaves the
  checksum to `checksum(src, dst, msg)` because it needs the IPv6 addresses; the hop-limit-255 rule
  is the caller's (it lives in the IPv6 header).

## Threat model / out of scope

A codec over untrusted, unauthenticated broadcast/multicast frames: the defense is
bounds-checking (every advertised length is validated against the buffer before it is read) so
hostile input yields a typed error, not a panic or out-of-bounds read. It does **not** authenticate
or validate the *semantics* of a frame — LLDP/CDP/ARP/DHCP are themselves unauthenticated
protocols, so a parsed neighbour/lease is a claim, not a verified fact (ARP-spoofing / rogue-DHCP
detection is the caller's policy). Out of scope: packet capture/injection (AF_PACKET, BPF), the
transmit scheduling of LLDP/CDP, DHCP state machines, and the checksum-secured integrity of any
protocol beyond the CDP checksum it computes.

## Verification

Each protocol has golden-byte KATs transcribed from the specs asserting the parsed typed model and
round-tripping build → parse, plus malformed/truncated-input negatives and a 1000-iteration
garbage-sweep (never panics). Run: `zig build test-l2disco`.

**2026-10-04:** an LLDP-MED phone advertisement, a DHCPACK carrying options 42/43/60/66/67/82/
119/121 and four ND messages (NS, NA, RA with MTU/prefix/RDNSS, RS) were built for the tests and
decoded by tcpdump 4.99.6 (`-vvv`); every expected value in the tests is what tcpdump printed
(and tcpdump's "icmp6 sum ok" anchors the ND checksum). Where tcpdump has no decoder — option 119
and the 802.3at power extension — the test cites RFC 3397 §2's own example and IEEE 802.3at
§79.3.2's layout instead. The builders reproduce the tcpdump-checked bytes. Mutation: 34 mutants (final set),
all killed, 4 of them only after new tests (reserved label types with enough bytes behind them,
width 33 with enough bytes, the full 4-bit MED priority, RA preference bits).

- **2026-10-31 (no-panic sweep GX):** caller-contract violations in the builders/accessors (`Mac.format` short buffer, `arp.Packet.encode` unequal/oversized address lengths, `dhcp.Builder.addRouters/addDnsServers/addNtpServers` bad list, `Ip4List.at`/`nd.Rdnss.at` out of range) are now checked `@panic`s with an `l2disco:` message in every build mode. Open question: turn the builder ones into `BuildError` members (`InvalidAddressList`, `InvalidAddressLength`) in a signature-changing pass. Not done: RFC 3396 concatenation of repeated long DHCP options (typed fields keep the last occurrence; the raw options stay reachable via `optionIterator`).

None recorded — no deferred-gap note beyond the general Linux-only-members-accepted
scope note (raw-syscall nature, not a functional gap), and the module README has no Deferred
section.

**Deliberately out of scope:** relaxing LLDP mandatory-TLV *ordering* (Chassis ID, Port ID, TTL
must appear first, in that order). A consumer that asked for `lldp.ParseOptions.tolerant_optionals`
separately flagged ordering as something it could imagine wanting relaxed too, but called it out as
its own, distinct decision rather than bundling it into the optional-TLV finding — so it was left
alone here. Revisit only on a fresh, explicit ask; do not fold it into `tolerant_optionals` as a
"while we're at it."

- **2026-10-04:** the three survey items below are **done**, except DHCPv6 (deferred: a separate
  message format and option space, roughly the size of the DHCPv4 codec; no consumer asks — axp's
  rogue-DHCP check is DHCPv4). Also deferred: LLDP-MED location content (civic-address CAtypes,
  coordinate LCI) — returned as `format` + bytes; builders for power/location/inventory TLVs
  (`Builder.addOrgSpecific` takes the raw info).
- ~~**LLDP-MED (TIA-1057) and 802.3at power-via-MDI decoding**~~ **DONE 2026-10-04** *(survey 2026-09-30)* — the org TLVs a VoIP-phone/PoE-switch neighbour advertises (capabilities, network policy, location, inventory, power). Small-medium (tables + bounds checks). Fits §2.
- ~~**More typed DHCPv4 options**~~ **DONE 2026-10-04** *(survey 2026-09-30)* — relay agent information (82), classless static routes (121), domain search (119), vendor-specific/class id (43/60), TFTP/boot file (66/67), NTP (42), plus `Builder` support for them. Small each. Fits §2.
- ~~**DHCPv6 and ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery codecs**~~ **DONE** *(survey 2026-09-30)* — ND 2026-10-04 (`nd`), DHCPv6 2026-11-04 (`dhcp6`, RFC 8415: header and relay header, option framing at parse, DUID, IA_NA/IA_TA/IA_PD with IA Address and IA Prefix, status code, option request, DNS/SNTP servers, domain list, `unwrap` for relay chains, `Builder`).
- ~~**LLDP-MED location content**~~ **DONE 2026-11-04** — `MedLocation.coordinate()` (RFC 3825), `civic()` (RFC 4776 elements) and `elin()`. Civic has no foreign decoder in our oracle (tcpdump 4.99.6 prints nothing for it); its layout is checked against RFC 4776 §3.1 by hand-built vectors only.
- **Deferred (2026-11-04):** DHCPv6 prefix-delegation exclude (67), vendor options (17) and Client FQDN (39) stay raw through `option(code)`; typed LLDP org TLV builders (power, location, inventory); RFC 3396 long-option concatenation for DHCPv4. A DHCPv6 *Authentication* (11) check is the caller's, like the other protocols' authenticity.

`gap · any · codec · reentrant` + deps: `netaddr` — canonical source is `pub const meta` in
src/root.zig.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — published vectors, goldens captured from a foreign implementation, or a test run against a live foreign peer.

**What the tests actually contain.** src/capture_test.zig runs 15 real LLDP/CDP/ARP/DHCP frames vendored from tcpdump's own dissector test suite (4 of them upstream crash reproducers) through these decoders (and the ARP encoder writes the real request back); since 2026-10-06 `src/tcpdump_oracle_test.zig` replays `tools/tcpdump_oracle.py`: 18 LLDP / CDP / DHCP / DHCPv6 frames built from the standards to reach every shape the decoders model (all chassis/port subtype families, TTL 0, IPv4+IPv6 management addresses, 802.1 PVID/PPVID/VLAN name, 802.3 MAC/PHY/power/max frame, LLDP-MED capabilities/policy/location/extended power/7 inventory fields, CDPv1+v2, DHCPv6 (message types, DUID-LLT/LL, IA_NA/IA_PD with addresses and prefixes, status, DNS/SNTP, domain list, option request, relay nesting), DHCP header fields and options 1/3/6/12/15/42/50-55/60/61/66/67/82/119/121) with 163 facts parsed out of tcpdump 4.99.6's own decode (2026-11-04: three DHCPv6 frames -- Solicit, a Reply with IA_NA/IA_PD/DNS/domain list, a relay-forward around a Solicit -- and an LLDP-MED coordinate LCI, whose 34-bit fields tcpdump prints unsigned) (option 119, which tcpdump leaves undecoded, from dnspython) -- the decoders must render the same facts, and the LLDP / CDP / DHCP Builders must reproduce the frames byte for byte. Not anchored: the CDP checksum of odd-length frames (tcpdump does not verify CDP checksums; the documented Cisco deviation stays as stated)

**How it got there.** The anchoring work landed. DONE 941bbfe: 15 tcpdump-suite frames incl. 4 upstream crash reproducers
